findings.reason: naming the record as `claim.json` and its `claim_registered_at` field, and saying why the existing attempt-claim reader cannot serve, is what stops the node implementing the fallback against the wrong claim file and shipping a gate that measures nothing.
findings.text: §19 states the falling-through case is one that "holds neither `attempt_started_at` nor an attempt record", but `_attempt_started_seconds` (`reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:495`) already dates from a third source: an `attempt-N.claim` file read by `_attempt_claim_seconds` (:625) through `_attempt_claim_path` (:578 → `resumption.attempt_claim_path`, which builds `attempt-{n}.claim`). The run §19 measures carries a different record — `claim.json` in the run directory holding `claim_registered_at` (verified in the measured run's own directory) — which no current reader consults, and which is exactly the record the Deliverable names. The distinction matters because the plan's phrasing sends a node to "the run's claim" without saying it is `claim.json` and not the `attempt-N.claim` reservation the liveness module already treats as the claim; a node wiring the fallback into `_attempt_started_from_claim` would produce no change for the measured shape, §19's first case would still read `running`, and the negative control would not distinguish the two

rubric_items.done_when: pass — each unit names a measurable test, a real negative control, a base arm and a suite delta; §19's control was confirmed by observation at HEAD (a datable cli pointer past the bound classifies `launch-failed`; the undatable measured shape classifies `running`), and §20's control removes the declared-path arm the first case depends on.

rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose reaches a symbol or path the units add; the session names ("nova-8a", "power-convertor-e5") appear only as the measurement's provenance in plan prose, not in code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §19's stated fall-through case omits the second claim record that already dates a run, so the account of what the attempt clock can reach does not match the code it cites.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §19 is one deliverable (date an undatable cli `starting` pointer and report it through `_stranded_launch`), and §20 is one deliverable (resolve a backend against a declared host search path), each closed by one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — neither §19 nor §20 declares a relationship, and neither needs one: §19's mechanism builds on the existing stranded-launch arm (`reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:746`, reached at `reckon/crew/recovery_classification.py:2065`) and §20 touches only the launch search path, so no missing or wrong dependency was found.
